correctness.rationale: Independent directed trajectories yield exact Q_s and factorial moments; Bonferroni truncations give o(log^-2 n) Poisson approximation for Z0, a birth-death supermartingale bounds post-first-jump early failure by O(log^-2 n), and the no-outside-incoming/internal-edge subset bound is O(log n/n). Together this proves O(log^-2 n) coupling error and sharp TV constant. The embedded checker passes 1265 exact finite assertions; it is not a proof for all n.

originality.rationale: 1990 Ball–Barbour already proves the general Poisson approximation with \(O(1/\log n)\) error and discusses early epidemic mixture; 2022 and 2024 frog papers study different regimes and/or initial populations. Checked primary texts and scientific-record searches did not show the exact coefficient-one TV asymptotic and \(O((\log n)^{-2})\) two-component approximation for the one-root model; priority remains conditional on older epidemic refinements.
residual_risks: General epidemic and random-digraph literature may contain an overlooked explicit higher-order survivor law despite the inspected 1990 upper bound and qualitative mixture remark.
The 2024 frog model has an additional root population; its coverage statements cannot be equated to the present one-root model.
The theorem is restricted to c fixed and one initial root frog.

value.rationale: Quantifies the concrete sharp constant missing in the known O(1/log n) Poisson error and isolates a rare catastrophic extinction mass at n-1 while the rest of the survivor law is Poisson to second order. The result supplies an informative critical finite-size correction to complete-graph epidemic coverage.
